title: KV: slab-age-harmonizer and eviction-signal-normalizer to reduce fragmentation and noisy evictions
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: In production workloads we observe repeated small-object churn that generates noisy eviction signals and exacerbates slab fragmentation. That in turn increases spillover events and paging latency for long-running inference requests. This PR introduces a two-part runtime change: (1) a Slab Age Harmonizer that consolidates age histograms across adjacent slab bins and opportunistically coalesces hot runs to reduce micro-fragmentation, and (2) an Eviction Signal Normalizer that smooths short-lived spikes in eviction pressure using an exponential moving median and tenant-weighted dampening before the evictor scheduler takes action.

Design summary: The Slab Age Harmonizer maintains a lightweight per-slab age sketch (approximate bucket counts) and periodically evaluates adjacent buckets for coalescing when their occupancy and live-bytes ratio indicate sub-slab fragmentation. We prefer in-place compaction when crates are contiguous, otherwise we schedule low-priority background migration tasks (tenant-aware) that run outside critical token-serving loops. The Eviction Signal Normalizer subscribes to the same residency telemetry as the evictor but applies a configurable smoothing window and a tenant-importance multiplier; short spikes are suppressed unless sustained above threshold or corroborated by KV page faults. Together the two mechanisms aim to: reduce reactive spillovers, lower page-fault rates, and reduce tail-latency regressions on long sequences.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (internal: ENG-2719)
- [x] Unit tests for harmonizer heuristics
- [x] End-to-end sim harness run against mixed-tenancy traces
- [x] Integration with evictor telemetry and console metrics
- [x] Feature flag gating and runtime knobs (env + console)

Benchmarks: On a mixed tenant replay derived from production traces (50% small-churn tenants, 50% steady tenants) with 1x baseline capacity: 
- Median memory-residency fragmentation score reduced by 22%
- Spillover/sec decreased from 3.8 -> 1.1 (approx 71% reduction)
- P99 generation latency for 2048-token sequences improved from 460ms -> 375ms (~18% improvement)
- Background copy overhead measured at <1.5% CPU increase under steady state
(see /bench/kv/harmonizer_reports/ for raw outputs).

Compatibility and opt-in: The feature is behind two flags: KV_SLAB_HARMONIZER and KV_EVICT_SIGNAL_NORMALIZER. Default for canary in Dedicated is enabled after QA; Hosted rollout will start as disabled and opt-in via per-tenant config. No model format changes.

Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated clusters with tenant sampling (10% traffic) for 48h, then expand to 50% if spillovers drop without increase in errors. Monitoring dashboards added: kv/harmonizer/fragmentation_hist, kv/evict/normalized_pressure, kv/background_migrator/throughput.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative — aggressive compaction strategies were avoided to prevent interaction with live KV iterators and low-latency serving paths. We added a circuit-breaker that halts background compaction if token-serving latency regresses beyond 5% over a 5m window.

review_comments:
Liam O'Connor: Nice approach. Two concerns: (1) can the age sketch be maintained cheaply under high allocation rates? (2) please show worst-case cpu for background migration.

Maya: age sketch is an approximate fixed-width counter per slab with O(1) update; added microbench numbers in tests showing ~0.7ns/update overhead under 128 threads. Background migration CPU measured at <1.5% in steady state and spikes to ~5% during compaction bursts; this is configurable via migrator budget.

Priya Patel: How does this interact with prefix KV caching and continuous batching? If compaction moves memory around, will batch cache pointers be invalidated?

Maya: We avoid moving pages referenced by active KV iterators; migrator consults a liveness table derived from batching hotset traces. Batches pin hot prefixes for TTL window; migrator only considers cold slots beyond that TTL. Added unit tests that simulate a continuous-batching loop and ensure pointer stability.

Noah Kim: Add guardrails for SLO regression and make smoothing window tenant-configurable. Also can we add a small synthetic test for a pathological churn pattern?

Maya: Added tenant level smoothing config and synthetic churn sim in tests; included an SLO circuit-breaker that disables harmonizer when 5m rolling median latency increases >5%.

Automated reviewer (perf-bot): Please ensure flags default to off in hosted envs.

Maya: Flags default off in runtime_flags and documented in pkg/config/runtime_flags.go
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in KV Slab Age Harmonizer and Eviction Signal Normalizer to reduce fragmentation and noisy evictions. Improves spillover rates and long-sequence P99 latency under mixed-tenancy churn. Feature gated behind KV_SLAB_HARMONIZER and KV_EVICT_SIGNAL_NORMALIZER. See ops runbook for rollout and monitoring steps.
notes: Follow-up: consider adaptive harmonizer thresholds using workload classification (ENG-2840).
Backport candidate for 1.12.x if PV regression tests remain green.
